status: complete source-grounded replacement proposal; awaiting independent script review before voice
spine: Why automated verdicts can acquire undeserved authority; how explicit criteria, executable evidence and evaluator tests make judgment inspectable; what readers gain by connecting engineering to appeal and governance.
readScope: Full original54-sentence script; complete source14,19,27,49,53; substantial17 with output truncation acknowledged; full section map. No claim of full word-for-word rereading.
durationIntent: About three minutes, measured after calm local narration; shorten content if needed, never accelerate speech.

evidence.quote: A code patch that fails its tests should not pass because the explanation is elegant.
A weighted average is particularly dangerous because it can allow excellence on soft criteria to compensate for a hard failure.
A patch can pass the existing suite while violating the intended requirement.
Once systems begin padding responses, the correlation fails.
A system that cannot abstain converts uncertainty into arbitrary authority.

scenes.title: What does a score permit?
lines: An elegant explanation cannot rescue a code patch that fails its tests.
Judgment Engines asks how automated evaluators can earn authority over decisions.
Its central claim is that reliable judgment requires an engineered procedure.
The book connects explicit standards, checked evidence, and the consequences of a verdict.
Readers learn to examine the evaluator before trusting what its scores permit.
scenes.art: Open on a particular proposed software change and its explanatory note on an illuminated inspection bench; a physical release latch remains closed. A visible failed test belongs to the change, while the elegant explanation remains beside it. This is the source’s conceptual example, not a claimed product test or measured benchmark. Indigo inspection tools, coral findings, ivory paper; no generic person flanked by icons.

scenes.title: Make failure decisive
lines: A flat average can let excellent presentation compensate for a critical failure.
The proposed alternative gives some criteria explicit dependencies or vetoes.
In the patch example, a failed test keeps release blocked.
Clarity can still be assessed without cancelling that functional failure.
The standard becomes an inspectable evaluation program, rather than a list of adjectives.
scenes.art: Macro view of the same change under two assessment mechanisms. The rejected flat-average sketch has no fabricated score. The revised physical release latch is controlled by the functional-test finding; prose quality remains an independent annotation. Move the failed result into the latch stop so its consequential role is visible, not a row of three label boxes.

scenes.title: Evidence before opinion
lines: The code chapters insist on running available checks before asking for opinions.
Tests provide behavioral evidence, but an existing suite can miss an important requirement.
Semantic review compares the change with its intended purpose and looks for missing cases.
These roles complement each other without turning the model into a pretend test runner.
The same division carries into evidence checking across the wider book.
scenes.art: Change scale to the actual workbench: a bounded test runner produces a recorded result for the patch. Then focus on requirement sheet beside an uncovered case, represented as an explicit open question without invented code behavior. Keep observed test result distinct from reviewer suggestion. Do not assert tests passed after merely changing a note.

scenes.title: Agreement can mislead
lines: The evaluator itself then needs tests designed to expose misleading shortcuts.
A writing judge may reward length because longer answers once happened to be better.
Padding can break that connection while the judge keeps agreeing with itself.
Repeatability therefore differs from measuring the quality the task actually requires.
Likewise, instructions inside a candidate must not acquire authority over its assessment.
scenes.art: Move from software bench to two answer strips with identical core content; extra filler lengthens one strip while a length-sensitive gauge responds. Mark this as a conceptual failure mode with no numeric accuracy. Reveal the repeated same verdict beside unchanged substance. End with an embedded instruction visually retained inside the candidate paper, never entering the separate rubric. No generic shield animation.

scenes.title: Keep judgment challengeable
lines: When evidence is missing, a useful judge can abstain and request further review.
A meaningful appeal preserves the evidence and rules needed to challenge a verdict.
The book develops these responsibilities across software, science, education, and institutional decisions.
Start with Rubric Engineering and Decomposition to see how standards become operational.
Then follow the harness and governance chapters to examine what happens after scoring.
Read it when choosing an evaluator also means deciding how much authority to delegate.
scenes.art: Return to the inspection bench from the affected contributor’s side. A missing-evidence case goes into an explicit review tray, while the original failure record and criterion remain retrievable for reconsideration. Final outside-reader view opens the real book to rubric and governance sections, with the latch still visible in the background as the question earned by the film. Avoid a universal approval stamp or magically repaired patch.

boundaries: Patch and writing examples are conceptual source examples, not new empirical results.
Failed known test and untested requirement remain distinct.
No fabricated numeric score, clinical instruction, deployed endpoint, or universal reliability claim.
Inspect all themes and actual visible motion; preserve source-qualified narration and one sentence per clip.
